Read `README.md` and current rollout evidence first. Produce exactly one multi-wake target-policy candidate in `solver/`. Keep candidate-specific reasoning in `logs/optimize/wake_policy_notes.md`, and add or materially revise at least one evidence-backed reusable lesson in `guidance/control_experience.md` from the assigned parent, sampled solver results, and inherited logs. If no positive lesson survives the evidence, record a concrete negative result and what later workers should avoid or test. The candidate is incomplete until both files are updated. Work only inside this Phase 2 workspace.

Use the fish-control bookshelf through this structured transfer protocol:

1. Before the first architecture proposal from the common naive seed, consult `guidance/skills/fish-control-primitives/SKILL.md` and its references.
2. On later iterations, consult it again when the inherited guidance indicates three consecutive completed iterations with neither a new controller mechanism nor a semantic improvement such as a new success, a better termination class, or a meaningfully different useful trajectory.
3. Consultation is required at those moments; adopting a primitive is optional. Do not use the shelf to justify scalar-only gain tuning.
4. If a source informs the edit, record a concise block in `logs/optimize/wake_policy_notes.md`:

```text
bookshelf_consulted: true
source_domain:
source_mechanism:
transferable_invariant:
nontransferable_details:
policy_translation:
falsification:
```

Translate only the invariant into normalized body-frame observations and the two-joint state-feedback contract. Prefer one mechanism or one small compatible combination. Published gains, species-specific kinematics, exact vortex phases, and task-specific routes are not transferable answers.

I’m starting with the workspace contract, inherited rollout evidence, and both relevant skills: the required fish-control bookshelf for mechanism transfer, plus the visual-signal skill because this policy change depends on the two moving-window views. I’ll keep all edits inside this Phase 2 workspace and will produce one candidate only.

The workspace confirms this is a first architecture proposal from the common seed, so the bookshelf consultation is mandatory. I’m now anchoring that transfer in the four sampled rollouts: parent guidance and inherited notes, score/termination summaries, metrics/diagnostics, and both rows of the combined keyframes—before proposing or editing any controller structure.

The sampled population gives a clear mechanism comparison: posterior-only mean curvature with bearing trend is the only candidate that materially improved approach (minimum distance 11.413L versus 12.078L for the seed) while retaining a coherent 3D wake, but every variant still curved into the upper boundary. The shared-body-bias version was especially harmful, ending at 13.411L after a large U-turn. I’m consulting the bookshelf now to choose a compact mechanism that addresses persistent yaw without turning this into scalar gain tuning.

The bookshelf points to half-cycle amplitude asymmetry for exactly this boundary: static mean curvature preserved thrust but did not brake the turn, while spreading mean curvature into joint 1 collapsed the traveling bend. I’m recording the pre-edit hypothesis now: preserve the best candidate’s target-bearing/trend loop, but translate it into a bounded posterior half-cycle asymmetry so the requested side of the beat gains authority without shifting the carrier’s equilibrium. The controller will also return accelerations inside the existing actuator envelope.

The policy is now a single mechanism-level candidate: the anterior oscillator is unchanged; only the posterior lagged target is asymmetrically scaled by target request and inferred beat side, with bounded target and returned acceleration. I’m updating the durable guidance to reflect what the evaluated first-generation comparison actually established—especially the partial success of posterior steering and the negative result for shifting joint 1.

The candidate, notes, and reusable guidance are all present, and there is exactly one `candidate_target_policy.jl` in `solver/`. I’m invoking the required lightweight check runner now; it will validate the guidance delta, policy schema/execution contract, and editable-file boundary without CFD.

The configured check-runner model is unavailable in this account, so its invocation failed before running any command. I’m using a plain validation worker with the same `.codex/agents/check-runner.toml` instructions as a compatibility fallback; the checks remain read-only and CFD-free.

The policy contract and editable-file boundary both pass. The guidance check exposed a rendered-workspace metadata defect: the same assigned parent is listed twice with the copied marker, so the checker stops before comparing guidance. I’m removing only that exact duplicate marker—without changing the parent identity or evidence—then I’ll rerun all three checks.

Completed exactly one policy candidate:

- [candidate_target_policy.jl](solver/cases/dogfish_3d_shape_policy/candidate_target_policy.jl): bounded posterior half-cycle asymmetry driven by body-frame bearing and bearing trend, preserving the anterior carrier.
- [wake_policy_notes.md](logs/optimize/wake_policy_notes.md): visual diagnosis, bookshelf transfer block, and falsification criteria.
- [control_experience.md](guidance/control_experience.md): reusable evidence-backed lessons on posterior-only steering and continuous-bias limitations.

All guidance, Julia contract, and repository-boundary checks pass. No CFD was run. I also removed an exact duplicate parent marker from `README.md` so the required guidance checker could resolve the unchanged assigned parent.
